q1: SELECT beer.name, min_price, bar FROM beer LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT beer, MIN(price) AS min_price FROM serves GROUP BY beer) AS t ON beer.name = t.beer LEFT OUTER JOIN serves ON beer.name = serves.beer AND min_price = serves.price
q2: SELECT b.name, min_price.price, s.bar FROM beer AS b LEFT JOIN Serves AS s ON b.name = s.beer LEFT JOIN (SELECT beer, MIN(price) AS price FROM Serves GROUP BY beer) AS min_price ON b.name = min_price.beer

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because of the order of JOIN operations and the placement of conditions in the WHERE clause. Q1 first performs the JOIN between beer and the subquery on serves, and then it performs the JOIN with the serves table again. Q2, on the other hand, first performs the JOIN between beer and the serves table, and then it performs the JOIN with the subquery on serves. This difference in the order of JOIN operations can lead to different results, especially when there are NULL values involved.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have a beer that is not served by any bar, and another beer that is served by multiple bars with different prices. The conditions that trigger the difference are the presence of NULL values in the min_price column and the order of JOIN operations.
